text:
maria: Quick sync  we need to finalize the priming_scope + evacuation hysteresis before the next canary. Two friction points: tenant-heavy priming causing noisy neighbors, and premature auto-evacuation on transient GC spikes.

sam: Agreed. Proposal: expose `priming_scope` and `priming_budget` per rollout. Default scope=tenant, budget=10% of tenant QPS or max 1000 reqs, whichever is smaller. That prevents global priming storms.

lee: Sounds reasonable. Also add a soft-evacuation state: `quarantine` before full `evacuate`. Quarantine routes new sessions away but lets in-flight finish; if metrics don't recover within `quarantine_window`, flip to `evacuate`.

jess: +1. We need hysteresis counters so flapping doesn't happen: require N consecutive windows failing (e.g. 3 windows of 60s) before quarantine, and then another M windows before full evacuate.

maria: Can someone sketch the rollout policy schema? I want the exact knobs for runbook and UI.

sam: Quick sketch (fields are illustrative):
```yaml
rollout_id: r-2026-07-priming
priming:
  scope: tenant        # tenant | global | explicit-tenant-list
  budget_per_tenant: 1000
  priority: low|normal|high
policy:
  detect_window_sec: 60
  consecutive_failures_to_quarantine: 3
  quarantine_window_sec: 180
  consecutive_failures_to_evict: 2
  grace_period_sec: 300    # don't auto-act until after this
  rollback_action: immediate|quarantine
telemetry:
  tag: x-rollout-phase
  span_name: rollout.step
  emit_metric_prefix: rollout.
```

lee: For the priming job we should also support a `dry_run` flag that exercises KV loads and metrics without actually touching live caches (read-only priming). That lets oncall validate cache hit behavior without affecting production eviction policies.

jess: For UI/runbook: show live counters: priming_budget_used, quarantine_count, last_transition_ts. Also expose a manual-override button: force-evacuate / cancel-evacuate with an audit comment.

maria: Who owns building the `quarantine` semantics in the router? Platform or runtime?

sam: Platform owns the decision surface (controller & config). Runtime/router implements the actions (steer new sessions, mark variant degraded). We'll add a small RPC: `POST /control/rollout/:id/transition` that runtime listens to.

lee: Runtime needs a well-defined contract for in-flight sessions. Suggest `drain_mode: allow_inflight|reject_new` and `max_drain_time_sec` to force kill after X.

jess: Also important: tie the auto-evacuation to a confidence signal. We should combine perf signals with eval-set regressions. One noisy signal shouldn't trigger quarantine. Use simple weighted scoring: perf*0.6 + eval_regression_score*0.4. Threshold param in policy.

maria: OK action items: sam prototype controller API + rollout schema, lee add dry_run mode to priming jobs and work with runtime for drain_mode, jess update runbook with UI elements and scoring formula.

deploy-bot: priming-job-14321 scheduled (scope=tenant, dry_run=true)

sam: I'll land a schema PR and mock the RPC in the router so we can demo.

lee: I'll add a small chaos test that simulates GC spikes to validate quarantine hysteresis.

maria: Great. Let's avoid making the initial defaults too aggressive; keep quarantine conservative. We'll run a dry-run demo with oncall tomorrow.

jess: I'll add dashboard panels and the manual-override control to the runbook so oncall can act fast.

maria: Thanks everyone. Short doc follow-up in the rollout README after PRs merge.
